Setup guide

How to play Eurovision Games in 60 seconds

A free, browser-based party game for the Eurovision Song Contest. Players predict the Top 5 and Worst 5, battle in head-to-head trivia duels, and chase five winner trophies — all while the show is on. No app, no account for guests, 2 to 20 players.

Setup in 60 seconds

One host signs in (magic-link email — no password). Everyone else joins from a link. The whole flow from empty browser tab to locked-in predictions is a single minute.

  1. Create the room (10s). Click Create Room. Pick quiz rounds (default 3) and max players (up to 20). A 6-character room code appears.
  2. Invite friends (20s). Share the code, the join link, and the auto-generated room password (included in the share message). Phone or laptop, any modern browser.
  3. Lock predictions (5 min before kick-off). Every player builds a Top 5 and Worst 5. Picks lock when the host advances past the predictions phase.
  4. Trivia warm-up. Quiz rounds run during the predictions phase as filler — points carry into the night total.
  5. Live show — duel time. Once the host advances to Live Show, quiz closes and duels open. Challenge anyone in the room.
  6. Trophy reveal. When results are entered, the room moves to Final and five winners are crowned.

Lock predictions

Predictions are the bedrock of the night — they score automatically the moment Eurovision results come in, so they reward homework and a bit of nerve.

  • Top 5. The five countries you think will finish 1–5 in the official combined ranking, in your predicted order.
  • Worst 5. The five countries you think will finish bottom of the leaderboard, ordered last-place first.
  • No overlap. A country can appear in only one list per player.
  • Order matters. An exact-position hit pays 50 points; a country that lands in the right list at the wrong rank pays 20.
  • Hard lock. Once the host advances past Predictions, no edits. Late joiners can still play trivia and duels but cannot enter predictions.

Trivia duels during the show

A duel is a 3-question Eurovision trivia battle between two players in the room. Questions fire on a 12-second timer; speed and accuracy both count.

How a duel plays out

Tap any other player’s name during the live show and choose Challenge. Both players answer the same 3 questions in private. The higher answer total wins the duel and pockets a flat +12 bonus. The winner then picks Steal (take points from the loser) or Double (add the same to themselves).

A default cap of 3 duels per pair (max 10), with rematches counted, prevents grinding one opponent for points all night. Refused challenges don’t count against the cap.

Live scoring

As Eurovision jury and televote results come in, predictions auto-score against the official combined ranking and the leaderboard updates instantly for everyone in the room.

  • Top 5 / Worst 5 score against the final combined ranking the moment results land.
  • Quiz points are banked from the predictions phase and never change.
  • Duel points swing in real time as duels resolve through the broadcast.
  • Either the host enters jury and televote results live, or they update automatically on grand-final night.

Five winner trophies

At the end of the night, five trophy cards reveal in sequence:

  • Champion — most total points across every phase. The headline title.
  • Thief — most points stolen via duel Steal effects.
  • Duelist — most duels won across the night.
  • Oracle — highest prediction-only score (Top 5 + Worst 5 totals).
  • Guru — most correct trivia answers across quiz and duels combined.

One player can win multiple trophies. Co-winners (2–5 tied) split a single trophy unless the host triggers sudden death.

Sudden-death tiebreak

For any tied trophy category, the host triggers a tiebreak vote — the room chooses Accept (co-winners share the trophy) or Sudden Death. Sudden Death only goes ahead if it wins a clear majority with at least 3 votes cast. If it does, the tied players enter a 3-question trivia match; most correct answers wins — speed breaks ties. If the vote stays with Accept, all tied players share the trophy.

What you need

  • A modern browser. Chrome 120+, Safari 17+, Firefox 121+, Edge 120+ — phone or desktop. PWA install on iOS and Android.
  • 2 to 20 players. Couples can share a single device.
  • The Eurovision broadcast. TV, official stream, or the EBU’s YouTube live feed — anything that lets you watch in real time.
  • No payment, no install, no account for guests. Only the host signs in.
